title: The branch root the legacy Pages builder republishes has no executive-summary banner, no phone pick index and no unresolved page
detail: Measured 2026-10-22T09:12Z with `python -m scripts.bc1afd8f_mobile_audit --root .` on the checked-in root: 8 of the 19 current-view checks fail. The root index.html has no `section.exec-banner`, carries zero `.glance-row` entries for the 17 active fixtures in `data/latest.json`, has no `unresolved/` directory at all, and keeps an orphan `twc-final/index.html` whose two tables are not inside any wrapper that declares `overflow-x:auto` (so they can stretch a 320 px phone page). `GET https://api.github.com/repos/buffedlizard55-lab/MaltaProj3/pages` answers `{"status":"building","build_type":"legacy","source":{"branch":"main","path":"/"}}` and `git show origin/main:data/latest.json` reads `generated_at 2026-10-15T08:36:13Z` with `counts.unresolved = 4`, so whenever that legacy build lands last a phone reader gets a week-old page with no pick index and no route to the unresolved register. The same audit run over a fresh build of the same code passes 20/20 (`data/research/bc1afd8f/mobile-audit-fresh-build.md`), so the gap is publication, not the renderer. `.github/workflows/pages-artifact-guard.yml` (this session) closes it from the side the repository controls: it re-deploys the newest verified artifact whenever the public site is not serving it, in a concurrency group that pushes to main cannot starve, and it commits nothing. Note on scope: `pages.yml`'s new `republish-last-verified` job (PR #183) re-deploys the last *verified artifact* on every push, and an artifact does contain the executive-summary banner, the phone pick index and `/unresolved/`, so this gap closes whenever a fresh build succeeds and the artifact deploy is the last one to land. It reopens on the next legacy root build, because the checked-in root still has neither. The two durable fixes are the root-sync publishing a self-consistent snapshot (see `bc1afd8f-root-publish-would-break-the-build`) or switching Pages off legacy publishing, which a workflow token cannot do (403).

title: RESOLVED on main (PR #183) — five consecutive four-hour refresh runs had been cancelled before their jobs started, and the scheduled 07:58Z slot was still queued 43 minutes later
detail: Read from the Actions API on 2026-10-22, not inferred. `pages.yml` keeps its whole refresh in one concurrency group (`pages`, `cancel-in-progress: false`); GitHub cancels a *pending* run in a group as soon as a newer run for that group is created. Run 39742916817 (PR #166 merge) was created 07:46:58Z and cancelled 07:47:40Z; 39742996589 (PR #167) created 07:47:38Z, cancelled 07:58:21Z; scheduled run 39744284108 created 07:58:19Z was still `queued` at 08:41:02Z; 39748026849 (PR #174) created 08:28:46Z, cancelled 08:29:01Z; 39748055891 (PR #176 - the very commit that added the root-sync step) created 08:29:00Z, cancelled 08:45:52Z when run 39750182735 arrived. With a dozen session PRs merging, the four-hour refresh the brief asks for can be starved indefinitely, and the root-sync step merged in PR #176 had never executed at all. RESOLVED while this session was measuring it: session 96fbe295 split the group per event name in PR #183 (commit 870f856, `group: pages-${{ github.event_name }}`), so a push can no longer cancel a pending scheduled refresh; the two independent observations agree on the mechanism and on the same cancelled run ids. The guard workflow this session adds now runs only on a schedule and on demand (its push trigger was removed at merge because `pages.yml`'s own `republish-last-verified` job covers pushes); it keeps its own concurrency group (`verified-artifact-guard`), re-deploys the newest verified snapshot when the public URL is not serving it, and dispatches `pages.yml` when the newest verified snapshot is older than the brief's eight-hour bound.

title: Committing a fresh snapshot into the branch root would break the build that every pull-request check and every refresh runs
detail: Reproduced offline, without touching the repository, by `python -m scripts.bc1afd8f_root_risk` (evidence: `data/research/bc1afd8f/root-publish-risk.md`, which now publishes two simulations side by side). `scripts/root_publish.py` publishes seven `DATA_FILES` into the branch root — `data/latest.json`, `data/origination.json`, `data/sources.json`, `data/row-source-audit.json`, `data/origination/aliases.json`, `data/evidence/hotspawn-fixtures.json` and `data/evidence/hotspawn-context.json` — and leaves the other 36 of the 38 committed files in `data/evidence/` frozen at 2026-10-15. Simulation 1 pairs the newest saved live snapshot (`data/research/fbdc97d6/live`, `generated_at 2026-10-22T02:08:59Z`) with the checked-in evidence tree: `scripts.validate.check_data` fails with `ValueError: Inventory observation timestamp restamped`, because it requires `data['inventory_observed_at'] == context['observed_at']` from `data/evidence/hotspawn-context.json`. Simulation 2 is the faithful one and runs on a GitHub runner after a real fresh build: it calls `root_publish`'s own `build_plan()`/`apply_plan()` against the built `site/` tree in a throwaway copy of the root, so the simulated root is byte-for-byte what a successful root-sync commit would leave on `main`, and then replays `check_data` on it (`python -m scripts.bc1afd8f_root_risk --site site`; result in the same report). Both simulations are anchored on `git archive HEAD data`, never on the working tree: the first runner run of simulation 2 reported a comfortable `passed` because this session's own workflow had already collected a fresh snapshot into `data/` before the step ran, so it compared fresh data with fresh evidence. The report now publishes where each base tree came from, which simulation was decisive, and why the other one was only a control. `checks.yml` runs that build on every pull request and `pages.yml` runs it before deploying, so a root that does not replay turns every PR red and freezes the refresh pipeline itself. 33 checked-in test modules also read `data/latest.json` or `ROOT/'data'` directly as their fixture. Change request for whoever owns `scripts/root_publish.py` / `pages.yml` (PRs #176 and #183; no file another session owns was edited here): publish the build's whole evidence tree instead of seven files. The committed evidence tree measures 38 files / 3.0 MB and a fresh build's own tree is measured in the same report (`site data/evidence/`); it is already inside the Pages artifact, so copying it into the root makes the committed snapshot self-consistent and keeps `check_data` green; committing it every four hours costs about 18 MB of repository growth a day, which is the real trade-off to decide. The durable alternative is to stop the branch root from being a publisher at all — `PUT /repos/.../pages {"build_type":"workflow"}` answers 403 from a workflow token, so that needs a human or an admin-scoped token. Until one of the two lands, `.github/workflows/pages-artifact-guard.yml` keeps the verified artifact on screen and commits nothing.

title: RESOLVED on main (PR #181) — the published snapshot is reconciled, so a byte-parity test had been failing for every session
detail: `tests/test_review_flags.py::test_render_only_findings_do_not_rewrite_the_canonical_json` asserts that `site/data/latest.json` is byte-identical to `data/latest.json`. `scripts.build.write_reconciled_snapshot()` (merged in PR #174) now republishes that file with `indent=1` plus `featured_method_counts`, `complete_coverage_counts` and `counts_note`, so the assertion cannot hold; the canonical source file itself is still untouched, which is the part that matters. Observed failing in run 39750731773 (this session's claim commit, i.e. main's own code), run 39749574716 (PR #178) and run 39749347079 (PR #171) through the check-run annotations API. PRs #164, #168, #171 and #173 already touch that test file, so this session deliberately did not edit it; it is recorded here so the red check was not mistaken for a regression introduced by this branch. RESOLVED while this session was working: session df80ab9f made `write_reconciled_snapshot()` preserve a byte-identical `latest.json` in PR #181 (commit 81139b1). Re-verified on this branch after merging `origin/main` at 2026-10-22T09:50Z: `python -m unittest tests.test_review_flags` reports 2 tests OK.

title: RESOLVED on main (PR #179) — today's live snapshot could not be built at all: the published tie-break for an exactly even research estimate was rejected by the complete-picks validator
detail: Measured on the runner from a live collection at 2026-10-22T09:15:53Z (104 inventory records, 43 active fixtures, every one of them carrying a pick). Fixture 1082926 (Isurus vs Hacha, CCT South America 2026 Series #7, starts 2026-10-23T22:00Z) has no reachable two-sided price - Polymarket event 1233768 was rejected because its order-book spread of 0.82 exceeds the 0.15 ceiling - so the last rung is the HLTV world-ranking research model, which publishes exactly equal points for both teams (published positions 215 and 229) and therefore exactly 0.500/0.500. PR #174's `ranked_tie_break()` gives such a row a *direction* from HLTV's own published order and records the rule on the quote, but `scripts/build_origination.validate_origination()` asserted `m['pick_index'] == selection(o['probabilities'])`, and `selection()` returns no side for an exactly even estimate. The whole build therefore died with `AssertionError: Fallback pick differs from its probabilities` (929 tests run against that fresh snapshot, 34 failing: `data/research/bc1afd8f/gate-fresh-snapshot.md`). Because `scripts.build()` renders the complete-picks page through that validator, any refresh whose ladder ends on an exactly even ranking model publishes nothing at all and `pages.yml` falls back to the last verified snapshot - the site silently stops updating while every check looks green. Fixed twice, independently, within the same hour — and only one of the two fixes was right. Session df80ab9f replayed `ranked_tie_break()` inside `validate_origination` in PR #179 (commit 1c1d87b). This session wrote its own `expected_pick_for()` replay from the runner failure alone, and the runner refuted it: run 39757283508 (evidence commit 10d8224, 09:56:52Z) still ended with `AssertionError: Fallback pick differs from its probabilities` at `scripts/build_origination.py:715`, because that replay looked for the tie-break record on `origination.quotes[0]` while `scripts/originate.py` writes it onto the origination row itself (`chosen['tie_break'] = tie_record`, and `chosen` *is* the published row — `quotes` keeps the untouched quote). Main's replay reads the row's own `family`, `inputs` and `tie_break`, which is the real shape, so at merge this branch kept main's file verbatim and deleted its own duplicate; the tie-break semantics themselves are already pinned by `tests/test_4c972a51_tiebreak.py` (8 tests) and `tests/test_df80ab9f_audit.py::test_validate_origination_replays_ranked_tie_break`. Both replays passed the frozen checked-in fixture locally, because that fixture contains no exactly-even row — only a live snapshot can tell them apart, which is what the session workflow is for. The blast radius measured on the runner: 945 tests, 34 failing in 18 modules, and `origination/index.html` (the complete-picks page) never written while `index.html` still linked to it (`data/research/bc1afd8f/build-outcome.json`). What this branch adds is the production row shape from the live fixture: `EvenTieBreakValidationTests` in `tests/test_bc1afd8f.py` (4 tests) asserts that HLTV's published positions 215/229 give fixture 1082926 side 0 with `rule='published-rank tie-break'` and no probability moved, that `selection()` alone still returns no side for that row, that a `family='market'` quote or a 0.62/0.38 estimate is never tie-broken, and that the merged validator is the only tie-break replay in `scripts/build_origination.py`. No probability, price or alias was changed by this session. The 253 tests in the ten checked-in modules that exercise `build_origination` still pass on the frozen fixture after the merge.
